tasks.title: Create Enhanced Card Component
tasks.description: Develop an enhanced card component with consistent styling, shadows, and variants to be used throughout the dashboard.
tasks.details:
The Enhanced Card Component system has been implemented with the following features:

1. Card variants: default, elevated, outlined, ghost
2. Card sizes: sm(p-4), md(p-6), lg(p-8)
3. Interactive states: hover, focus, active
4. Accessibility support: role, tabIndex, aria-disabled, aria-busy
5. Keyboard navigation support (Enter, Space)
6. Loading state support (spinner animation)
7. Disabled state support
8. Component structure:
   - EnhancedCard: Base card container
   - EnhancedCardHeader: Header section (with bordered option)
   - EnhancedCardTitle: Title (supports levels 1-4, uses design token typography)
   - EnhancedCardDescription: Description text
   - EnhancedCardContent: Body content (with noPadding option)
   - EnhancedCardFooter: Footer section (with 4 alignment options)
9. Special card components:
   - StatsCard: For displaying statistics (title, value, change rate, icon)
   - FeatureCard: For feature introductions (title, description, icon, action)
10. Design token integration:
    - Uses colors, spacing, shadows, borders tokens
    - CSS variable-based styling (.rounded-card, .shadow-card)
    - Full typography system integration (.text-h1~h4, .text-body, etc.)
11. Added card styles to globals.css:
    - .rounded-card (var(--radius-md))
    - .shadow-card (var(--shadow-md))
    - .shadow-card-hover (var(--shadow-lg))
12. TypeScript type safety:
    - All props have defined types
    - React.forwardRef support
    - Extensible interface structure

tasks.title: Create Modal Component System
tasks.description: Develop a standardized modal component system with consistent header, body, and footer styling as specified in the PRD.
tasks.details:
1. Create a base Modal component with standardized structure 2. Implement consistent header with title and close button 3. Create standardized body section with proper padding 4. Develop footer with consistent button placement 5. Add animations for opening/closing 6. Implement backdrop and focus management 7. Support different sizes (small, medium, large) Example implementation: ```typescript // components/ui/modal.tsx interface ModalProps { isOpen: boolean; onClose: () => void; title: string; size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'; children: React.ReactNode; footer?: React.ReactNode; } export function Modal({ isOpen, onClose, title, size = 'md', children, footer }: ModalProps) { if (!isOpen) return null; return (

{title}

{children}
{footer && (
{footer}
)}
); } ``` ## Implementation Complete The Modal Component System has been successfully implemented with the following components: 1. **EnhancedModal** - Based on shadcn/ui Dialog with extended functionality - Size options: xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, full - Variants: default, elevated, centered, fullscreen - Full accessibility support: escape key, overlay click, focus management 2. **ConfirmationModal** - Includes confirm/cancel buttons - Supports destructive actions - Handles loading states 3. **InfoModal** - Simple modal for displaying information - Single confirmation button 4. **FormModal** - Specialized for form submissions - Automatic form tag handling - Submission state management - Cancel/save button combination 5. **LoadingModal** - Dedicated loading state modal - Cannot be closed during processing - Spinner animation 6. **useModal Hook** - State management: open, setOpen, openModal, closeModal, toggleModal - Clean React-based state management All components fully integrate design tokens (colors, spacing, shadows, borders, animations) and include complete TypeScript support, React.forwardRef implementation, ARIA accessibility, focus management, backdrop blur effects, responsive sizing, and Korean UI text. Required CSS classes have been added to globals.css.

subtasks.details:

- PRD breakpoints (sm: 640px, md: 768px, lg: 1024px, xl: 1280px)
- CSS variables for breakpoints
- Responsive container system (.container, .container-fluid)
- Complete responsive grid system (grid-cols, col-span for all breakpoints)
- Responsive visibility classes (sm:hidden, md:block, etc.)
- Responsive flexbox utilities (flex-row, flex-col)
- Responsive text alignment (text-left, text-center, text-right)
- Responsive width utilities (w-full, w-1/2, etc.)
- Layout variant classes (layout-sidebar, layout-two-column, layout-three-column)
- Max-width utilities (max-w-xs ~ max-w-7xl)
- Responsive overflow control (overflow-hidden, overflow-auto, etc.)
- Responsive height utilities (h-full, min-h-screen, etc.)

tasks.title: Perform Comprehensive Testing and Validation
tasks.description: Conduct thorough testing of the entire modernized UI to ensure all functionality is preserved and the design is consistent.
tasks.details:
1. Create a comprehensive test plan covering all components and interactions
2. Test all user flows and scenarios
3. Verify that all existing functionality works exactly as before
4. Validate responsive behavior across different devices
5. Test accessibility compliance
6. Perform visual regression testing
7. Conduct user acceptance testing

Test plan outline:
1. **Component Testing**
   - Test each component in isolation
   - Verify all props and configurations
   - Test edge cases (empty states, error states, etc.)

2. **Integration Testing**
   - Test component interactions
   - Verify data flow between components
   - Test modal opening/closing and data passing

3. **Functional Testing**
   - Test all user flows (adding/editing/deleting data)
   - Verify form submissions and validations
   - Test filtering and sorting functionality

4. **Responsive Testing**
   - Test on mobile devices (various sizes)
   - Test on tablets
   - Test on desktop (various sizes)
   - Verify layout adjustments at breakpoints

5. **Accessibility Testing**
   - Test keyboard navigation
   - Test with screen readers
   - Verify ARIA attributes
   - Check color contrast

6. **Visual Testing**
   - Compare before/after screenshots
   - Verify design consistency
   - Check for visual regressions

7. **Performance Testing**
   - Measure load times
   - Test animation smoothness
   - Verify bundle size optimization
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Create a test matrix covering all components and features
2. Use automated testing tools where possible
3. Perform manual testing for visual and UX aspects
4. Test across multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
5. Test on real devices for mobile and tablet views
6. Document and track all issues found
7. Verify that all critical functionality works as expected
8. Conduct regression testing after fixing any issues
